headline: Risk gauge lifts from Risk off to Mixed as Europe rallies on a milder tariff reading

findings.headline: Europe extends the rebound and the risk gauge moves back to Mixed
findings.body: By 09:45 Zurich the Euro Stoxx 50 was about 2% higher at 6,011 and VIX had eased about 5% to 26.8, lifting the risk on/off gauge from Risk off to Mixed (-9, from -25 at Wednesday night's reading). Breadth and lower volatility did most of the work; S&P 500 futures are up about 0.6%, the Bund 10-year yield is about 3bp higher at 3.25% and EUR/USD is flat near 1.097, so the move is equity-led rather than a broad macro shift. A Reuters report that the new US tariff rates will not be stacked on the July levies and are not expected before February or March is the main help, with banks and tech leading. US cash markets are shut for Thanksgiving, so liquidity is thin and New York has not tested the move.

findings.headline: German consumer climate barely improved, and is not driving the open
findings.body: The NIM Consumer Climate, powered by GfK, rose 0.7 points to -30.2 for December, slightly below the -29.9 average in a Reuters poll, and Rolf Bürkl said it was stagnating at a low level with little help for Christmas spending. Economic expectations fell, ending six months of gains, while price expectations ticked up. This print does not explain the equity bounce; this afternoon's events are the ECB's October account at 13:30 Zurich, the Bank of England's Financial Stability Report, and a scheduled appearance by Christine Lagarde.

findings.headline: Oil holds its Gulf premium into Sunday, with fresh Hormuz mine claims
findings.body: Crude is little changed around Europe's open after Wednesday's jump, still carrying a risk premium after the Houthi claim on Ras Tanura. Iran's state media said oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, a further threat to the recent recovery in Gulf shipments, and there is no WTI settlement today because of Thanksgiving. The 29 November OPEC+ meetings remain the next test, with the UAE outside the group and Iraq and Kazakhstan pressing for higher capacity estimates.

view: Our view: Europe has endorsed Asia's rebound at the open, and the milder tariff reading is the main change in tone since early morning; it is still a holiday-thin session with no US cash lead, so the bounce can fade as easily as it arrived. German consumers are not about to drive a spending revival. Oil is holding, not fading, into OPEC+ on Sunday.
